accuracy.evidence: Covers the three evidence statements of the topic: wondering aloud with 'maybe' and 'what if' (thinking cloud of three possible explanations for a vanished puddle, all physically plausible: evaporation, soaking into soil, an animal drinking), trying new vocabulary in talk (enormous, tiny, soggy matched to pictures and defined as very very big, very very small, wet and soft), and exploring ideas before committing (several maybes before testing). Wording follows the statutory spoken-language aim 'use spoken language to develop understanding through speculating, hypothesising, imagining and exploring ideas'. The ice test only claims sun melts faster than shade and a freezer keeps ice frozen, which is correct.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the real ways young children shut down exploratory talk: stopping at the first idea or saying 'I don't know' (the zip-mouth card is refused, challenge 'one'/'stop'), circular reasons that restate the question ('because his coat is wet', 'because it fell down', challenge 'again'), reasons that are not clues ('because it is Tuesday', 'because towers are red', 'because grass is green'), answering about yourself ('I like ice cream', 'I am not hungry'), and blocking a partner's idea with 'No, dens are silly' instead of building on it (challenge 'no'). The ice step targets the belief that ice melts anywhere.

lab_distinct.evidence: Mechanics belong to exploratory talk: a thought cloud that collects several competing maybes before any answer; a because-chooser judged against a drawn clue (rain cloud, a toppled tower beside a dog's tail, hot sun); a draggable ice cube tested in three places with a melting animation to turn a what-if into an observation; word cards dragged onto pictures; and a den that is drawn piece by piece only when a reply adds to a friend's idea. The distinctness gate passed against every flagship lab, including flaglisten, flagqw and flagmood.

lab_teaches.evidence: Each rule is discovered by doing: the cloud fills with three maybes and the lab says all could be true, so more than one idea is shown to be useful; circular and clue-free reasons are rejected with the specific slip named; the child predicts the freezer, drops the ice there and sees it stay solid while the sun turns it to a puddle; the den visibly gains a roof, torch light and a picnic only through 'yes, and', 'maybe' and 'what if' replies. The text after each task names the move just used.

predictions.evidence: Three locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option the lab disproves: 'Pip has one idea. Should Pip stop thinking? Yes, one is enough' (the next screen shows three plausible maybes), 'What if the ice goes in the freezer? Yes, it melts' (the freezer ice stays full size while sun ice melts away), and 'Leo says No, dens are silly. Does that help? Yes' (the 'No' reply is refused and the den does not grow).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating challenge kinds (more ideas, a real reason, what-if freezer, new word, adding to an idea, wondering words) with shuffled answers. Each wrong answer names its slip: 'One idea is a start. Say maybe and find more', 'That just says it again. A reason says why', 'Green is not why it is wet. Use a clue', 'The freezer is very cold, so it stays frozen', 'Tiny means very, very small', 'No stops the idea. Add to it with yes, and', 'That is not about the boat'. Lab steps add their own messages, e.g. 'Tuesday is not a clue. Look at the picture.'

readability.evidence: Kid paragraphs score FK 0.0 (family limit 5.0): short sentences, words such as maybe, because, what if, try, see. Adult text scores FK 8.6. Every lab instruction is one short line; meaning is carried by pictures (puddle before and after, rain cloud, melting ice, balls of two sizes, the growing den) so a pre-reader can play with an adult reading aloud. The lab uses the young class for 56 px buttons and larger step text.

no_filler.evidence: Kid paragraphs each teach one move (many maybes, because with a clue, test a what-if, new words and yes-and). Adult paragraphs give the curriculum link, what each lab step practises, named common mistakes, and a home routine. The five lab steps practise five different talk moves and none repeats another; the sorter is a separate quick check of helpful versus blocking phrases.

mobile.evidence: Checked iPhone 13 (390 px) screenshots in dark and light themes for every step before and after Show me. The first check showed the puddle question clipped by the thought cloud, so it moved to a full-width top line; the because clue was enlarged; the finished den was clipped at the left edge and overlapped its caption, so it is now centred with the caption below. Choice bars are full width and about 54 px tall, word cards about 56 px, and every canvas action has a 56 px button twin.

accessibility.evidence: Everything is doable with buttons: each idea card, each because, 'Ice in the sun/shade/freezer', word buttons with aria-pressed plus 'Picture 1-3' buttons whose aria-labels describe the picture ('a very small ball', 'a biscuit in milk'), and each den reply. The canvas aria-label is rewritten after every action with the question, progress and result (e.g. 'Freezer: It stays ice!'). The challenge feedback uses a polite live region, and the walkthrough's axe run (WCAG 2.1 AA) was clean in both themes on desktop and iPhone 13.
